description: A formal vocabulary for a domain: classes, properties connecting them, and constraints every fact must satisfy. The schema of a knowledge graph, plus meaning.
A hierarchy of terms (`Manager` is a kind of `Employee`). Useful for navigation; it has no relationships or constraints beyond the hierarchy.
The inheritance link between classes. Instances of a subclass are instances of the parent, and properties of the parent apply to the subclass.
A property's domain is the class of its subject; its range is the datatype of its value or the class of its target.
How many values each instance has for a property: `min 1` makes it required, `max 1` makes it single-valued.
Missing facts are unknown, not false. OWL reasoners use domain and range to infer types, not to reject data.
Data that breaks the rules is reported as a violation. SHACL does this for RDF; schema constraints and code do it for property graphs.
The questions an ontology must answer. They decide which classes and relations to model first.
